\revision{revival-integers}{The Working Draft of February 2011 declared
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} and of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}^*}; it typed
the result of division as \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^{\#}}, the power's exponent, the results
of the factorial, of \OPR{CHOOSE} and of the four hyperfloor and hyperceiling
operators as \EXP{\mathbb{N}}, the argument of \OPR{CMP} as \EXP{\mathbb{Z}^*}, and
the absolute value as \EXP{\mathbb{Z}_{\geq}}, and it declared twelve check
methods, each returning a refined type or throwing \TYP{CastError}.
The listing and the method entries below extend \TYP{Number} in place of
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}^*}, declare the coercions from the four
fixed-size integer types, and take \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} or \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} where
the original named a refined type; the check methods leave, since \library\
declare none on the integer types.
The sentences about the infinities of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}^*} and
\EXP{\mathbb{N}^*} leave the method entries, and so does the sentence that
declared the positive integers a type of their own, ordered by divisibility.
The coercions from the fixed-size integer types are new, with the method entry
that follows.
The exponent of the power, \EXP{\mathbb{N}} in the Working Draft, is now
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, so a negative power is admitted.
The Working Draft gave the result of a negative power through the
exponentiation of \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, since \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} was a subtype of
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}}: \EXP{2^{-1}} was \EXP{1/2}.
This chapter does not give it. The method entries of the three unary negations gave the result \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} where the listing gave \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}; on the flat tower that would make the negative of an integer a rational, and they now give \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, as the listing does.}

\subsection{The integer trait}
\seclabel{revival-integers}

\item[Rationale] \secref{revival-numbers}.
\Library\ declare no infinite integer and no check on the integer types.
Division takes the type the library declares for it; the other signatures take
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, since the library declares none of those methods with a
natural-number type (its power on integers is another method, returning a
floating-point value). Route~A gives each number type its own algebra, and the listing's commutative ring over \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} negates within \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}; the method entries' \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} held of an integer only while \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} was a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}.
\item[Effect] As \secref{revival-numbers}.
The integer types no longer hold infinities, so their total order is that of the
finite integers. Negating an integer gives an integer.
The exponent of the power, \EXP{\mathbb{N}} in the Working Draft, is now
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, so a negative power is admitted.
The Working Draft gave the result of a negative power through the
exponentiation of \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, since \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} was a subtype of
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}}: \EXP{2^{-1}} was \EXP{1/2}
(\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/numbers.tex}, lines 344--355).
The revised text of \secref{basic-integers} does not give it.

268	## 4. `QQ`'s body: the library's own way
269	
270	`AnyIntegral` comprises `{ZZ, ZZ64, ZZ32, NN64, NN32}` and declares no `-` and no `<` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:441-443`). The library handles "any integer" in Fortress text with a `typecase` over the comprised types: `exactValue` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:398-408`) and `Number`'s `=` (`:386-395`). In that shape, the body splits by the sign inside each type, and negates only within a signed type, so no unsigned value is ever negated:
271	
272	```
273	    opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral):QQ =
274	        typecase other of
275	            e: NN32 => (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e
276	            e: NN64 => (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e
277	            e: ZZ32 => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(-(widen(e))) else (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e end
278	            e: ZZ64 => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(-e) else (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e end
279	            e: ZZ => if e < 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(-e) else (numerator(self))^e / (denominator(self))^e end
280	        end
281	```
282	
283	- **Cost:** 8 lines for 6. The checker has no exhaustiveness check on a `typecase` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:676`, "TODO: A nonexhaustive typecase is an error"), and gives it the union of its arms, `QQ`.

## The principle for the batches

Every batch lands with the specification, the library and both paths agreeing. So the work is grouped by what has to change together, not split finer.

Two rules of the batch machinery shape the order: two rungs in one batch may not change the same declaration, and a rung cannot build on another rung of its own batch, since every rung branches from the batch's base (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:465`, batch rule 1). That is why the wrapping operators and the flattening sit in different batches, and why rung O's check follows the operators.

How a phase-3 batch's content is chosen (the coordinator's method, as batch 10 was planned): the measure is the distance, the compiled checker's errors on the one library, and the source is the last landed gate's per-site list (`compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`), every error with its site and class. The planner, an Opus worker, sorts it into three piles: (1) decided and free to fix, the library's one-off slips and the checker's defects with a known fix, which go into the batch; (2) waiting on a decision of Pavol's or a judgement (after batch 9: the arrays, 98, after the switch-over by his answer to batch 8's Q4; the self-typed bodies, 30, a list of ways and a judgement first; `isLeftZero` and items 37 to 42, his), which are held and listed in the record; (3) waiting on a probe, which is probed before the record is written (P1 for row 424's F-bounded half). Pile 1 gains the defects

## Preparing a batch record

An Opus planning worker drafts `CLIMB-BATCH-<n>.md`. A Fable reviewer edits it in place with one reason per change. The coordinator reads the diff and brings the record's questions to the curator one per message. The batch launches on the answers or on the standing go (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The go").

The planner builds each rung's briefing as in-context learning: the agents were not trained on Fortress, and the language was never finished (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The workflow"). A briefing holds what the rung's section cites: the decisions and earlier rulings it rests on, its ledger rows, the specification's sections whole by their headings, the notes on the subject by section, and the library code that is the precedent. Process positions and harness facts stay out, because the brief's role text and the skill carry them. In batch 10 the workers named none of the 87 POSITIONS and FACTS keys before their fix edits (`process-engineering/context-study.md`, section 5

A rung that changes what an implementation does is briefed with the Appendix I Effects and the specification's notes that its change makes false, found by a grep while the record is prepared. Batch 9's record gave rung K none, and Appendix I's `comprises` Effect was that batch's one blocking finding (`reviews/batch-9-review.md`, finding 3).

A record asks a rung for no corpus-wide output comparison, no ladder before-run, no microGPT check and no specification build log (P-103, "The suite's verdict is the check."; the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "What a brief holds"). Whole suites are the skill's rule (`tests-running.md`, "When to run a whole suite"). A count of the programs a change reaches, when a decision needs one, is the planner's probe, taken before the record is written. A named one-time count of changed outputs is asked only where a decision of the curator's names it for that rung. The coordinator starts its base pass before the launch (`tools/count-run/count-run.sh`).

The record's section on how it is run gives the manifest's fields rung by rung, the intro every agent reads, and the launch steps. It holds no copy of the block: the batch's generator writes the block from the record.

## Before the launch

The coordinator, in this order:

1. The script, this manual and the batch's manifest generator on `main`. The base is `main`'s head after them, by its full hash, passed as `args.base`.
2. The batch's one base build, a worktree at the base outside the main tree, built once and then left alone. Every rung worktree is seeded from it, and the old code runs from it (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The workflow"). About 200 s, as the skill's `worktrees.md`, "Finding or building a base build", gives it:

        git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add --detach /home/user/fortress-base<N> <base>
        cd /home/user/fortress-base<N>      # then set up the call as the skill's build-and-caches.md says
        ant compileAll                      # BUILD SUCCESSFUL
        # the library order (build-and-caches.md, "The library order"), then one walk run, which warms walk's caches:
        bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss
        git status --porcelain              # empty: the seed refuses a base build that is not clean

   Its path goes to the launch as `args.baseBuild`. The script refuses to start without it (scenario B1).
3. One trial seed proves the base build, about 3 s: `explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck - <base>`, then `git -C /home/user/fortress worktree remove /home/user/fortress-seedcheck`. One `old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck-caches ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss`, run from the main tree, proves the old code runs; its folder is removed after.
4. The briefings checked on the base (`python3 explorations/compile-ladder/plan-<N>/manifest/lists<N>.py`). The block generated (`gen<N>.py`), checked in a scratch copy and spliced (`check<N>.js`, then `check<N>.js --write`). Then `node explorations/coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js` on the spliced script, which also checks that every skill section the script cites by name is a heading of the skill. Then the commit.
5. `df -h /` against one seeded worktree per rung (about 206 MB each) and the base build. `git status --porcelain` empty in the main tree, and no other agent writing there or pushing `main` while the run gathers and commits. The session's permission rules let the commit stage run `tools/mg-run.sh`.
6. Check-ins armed for the run's length, 45 minutes apart (the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "Watching a run").

The launch: `Workflow({scriptPath: 'explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js', args: {base: '<full hash>', baseBuild: '/home/user/fortress-base<N>'}})`. The args are kept byte for byte, since a resume needs them. The base build stays until the coordinator removes it after the landing.

# Review of climb batch 20's record, before the launch

## 1. For the curator

**Verdict: ready to launch.** The record describes the tree it was drafted against. Rung I builds P-153 word for word: every integer `^` answers its own type, `IntegerOverflow` where the result is no integer, `DivisionByZero` at a base of 0, the bases 1 and -1 exact, a fraction from a float or rational base. Rung A builds P-40's diff on the 17 operators and nothing beyond them, with the library's own `cast` and leaf `fill` and `tabulate` for the other 20 sites. The arithmetic holds: 31 less A's 20 less I's 6 is 5, and 28 less 19 less 6 is 3; what stays is the second export error, row 731's 3 and item 46's 1. No line of microGPT changes, and both probes measured its quick pair equal. One miss is fixed: a third team demo, `npbft`, writes `10^(-6)` as the two named ones write `10^(-4)`, and it now goes with them. The three patches apply to `main` alone and together in the gather's order; the manifest generates and checks clean from the fixed record; the scenario checker passes. Nothing in the record reverses a decision of yours.

**The changes made, in the record and one reason line of `lists20.py` (one more line in `INDEX.md`):**

- `demos/npbft.fss:130`, `alpha = 10^(-6)`, joins fork 15 and rung I: the same line in the same shape as the two demos P-153 names, missed by the probe's reading of the demos. Rung I respells it `10.0^(-6)`, runs it once and lists it with its before and after.
- Fork 19 and section 4 cite `Constructor.boundsUnread` as `:722-737`, where it ends; the record said `:722-738`.
- Fork 11's rule for an exponent beyond 64 bits now says what a base of 0 gives at each sign: 0 at a positive exponent, `DivisionByZero` at a negative one. The record's "0, 1 and -1 exact" left the negative case open.
- `lists20.py`'s reason for F-247 names the third demo, so the worker's brief does not say "two".
- One sentence in the record's header names this review and its changes, in the form climb batch 19's record used.
- `INDEX.md` has this review's line.

**The one question near the batch, with its default. It does not hold the launch.**

- P-153 says "two demos written with a float base", and F-247 names `BiCGSTAB` and `BiCGSTAB2` by reading. The tree holds a third, `npbft.fss:130`. After rung I, that line raises `IntegerOverflow` under walk where it answers `0.000001` today.
- Default, taken: the third demo is respelled as the two, `10.0^(-6)`, and the line goes on your review list with its before and after, like theirs. The alternative is to leave the demo as it is and let it raise when it is run; no suite runs it.
- Why the default: your reason for the respelling, a program that wants a fraction writes a float base, applies to this line as to the other five. It is one team line, reversible, and no suite's verdict depends on it.

**The defaults the batch takes, on your review list.** None is consequential by the rules: none reverses or bends a decision of yours, none touches microGPT, each is settled by the record, the text or the library's way, and each can be undone.

- `IntLiteral`'s `^` answers `IntLiteral` (fork 10). Under walk a numeral is a `ZZ32` value, so `2^(-1)` reaches `Int$Pow` and raises as P-153 says. On the checker a numeral is `IntLiteral` (F-262), so `2^(-1)` reaches `IntLiteral$Pow`, which raises too, and `1^(-1)` is `1`, an `IntLiteral`, which every number type converts from. The compiled path's own library still answers `0` there, and a raw exception at a base of 0, until phase 4's natives (rows 441, 523): the rung does not touch it, and fork 13 says so.
- `MultiplicativeRing`'s api power `abstract` over `AnyIntegral`, with `RR64`'s api stating its component's `^` over `AnyIntegral` (fork 7). The api already writes `abstract` for the trait's other two bodiless members, `one` and `TIMES`; `AnyIntegral` is row 445's own fix for this trait and for `QQ` (fork 8). No program's answer moves: walk runs the component, which has these already; the checker reads its own library until the switch-over, and after it a wider exponent type and a stated declaration refuse nothing that passed. Measured: nothing comes, and the second export error loses the entry, 44 to 43.
- The api's two `immutableArray` ranks put in a comment (fork 5). The team's own component has had them in a comment since its last commit, and no `ImmutableArray2` or `ImmutableArray3` exists in the library, so no program can call them. P-40 builds the diff "with the array sites' other fixes", and the first export error clears only with both. Removing the comment brings the two lines back. Two factories leave Part IV: a point to report, as the record lists it.
- The second export error out, for a probe to the check's end (fork 18). The check names one member a trait, so the 43 entries left hide how many lines the mechanical part needs; and one `abstract` line in an api can bring a new error in another component, as the planner measured twice. Right to hold.
- Row 774 out, for a probe first (fork 19). P-154 lists walk's half as still to build, but no probe has said which walk tests move, and walk's reading of a `where` clause at an instance is not designed. It moves no site. Right to hold; the probe should design the read as well as count the moved tests.
- The team tests and demos respelled with a float base (fork 15): `realArith` twice, `compoundArray` six lines, `simpleExp` three, the three demos one each; each line with its before and after on your list. `simpleExp`'s comment, "that Int and Long exponentiation work (largely) as expected", stays though its bases become floats; the rung's own walk test checks the integer bases.
- The rest, each settled as the record says: two rungs, I and A (forks 1 to 3); the array ways as the patch has them (fork 4); the guard at all eight element types (fork 6); `QQ`'s `typecase` body (fork 9); the exponent read at any integer type (fork 11); row 747's gated test (fork 12); row 441 half fixed (fork 13); `DivisionByZero`'s name a constant (fork 14); the specification's sentences for E (fork 16); no speed pass (fork 17); nothing declared (fork 20).

**Three notes for the coordinator, outside this review's files:** F-247 and P-153's "Still to build" say two demos; rewrite F-247 at the landing with `record.py` (the record's "After the landing" already consolidates it by I), and narrow P-153's line as planned. `not_passing_yet/tree.fss:54-73` writes twenty `10^(-1)` scales in the same shape; no suite runs that folder, so the batch leaves it, and it meets the contract if it ever runs. The base build at `/home/user/fortress-base20` does not exist yet, as the record's step 3 says; the probe worktree is clean on `wip/probe-array-sites` at `7ab0e18eb`.

## 2. The changes, one reason each

1. **`npbft.fss:130` joins fork 15 and rung I** (section 1's rung bullet and cost; fork 15; "Team lines changed"; rung I's "The answers this rung follows", "The demos" and "Files"; the manifest's blurb and points; the intro; `lists20.py`'s reason for F-247). A grep of every `.fss` in the tree for an integer base at a negative exponent (`[0-9)]\^(-`) finds the record's eleven lines, `RationalTest`'s six rational bases, `not_passing_yet/tree.fss`, and `ProjectFortress/demos/npbft.fss:130`: `alpha = 10^(-6)`. The probe's section 1.5 lists `npbft.fss:14`, `a:ZZ64 = 5^13`, among the integer uses and nothing at `:130`; F-247 and P-153 follow it. The line is reached: `run()` calls `dobenchmark(2, 4, 4, 1)` (`:146-148`), and `alpha` scales the exponent of `e`, an `RR64` (`:54`, `:136`). Today `Int$Pow`'s negative branch answers a float (`Int.java:224-226`); after rung I it raises. The file declares its own `Complex` object (`:36`), so it does not wait on the complex numbers the specification leaves unbuilt.
2. **`Constructor.boundsUnread` is `:722-737`** (fork 19; section 4, "Held"). Its comment opens at `:722` and the method's closing brace is at `:737`; `:738` is blank, and `:739` opens the next comment. Row 774 cites `:725-737` at an earlier commit.
3. **Fork 11's rule for an exponent beyond 64 bits.** The record said "(0, 1 and -1 exact, IntegerOverflow at any other base)". At a negative exponent a base of 0 is a division by zero, not 0, by P-153; the new parenthetical says 0 at a positive exponent and `DivisionByZero` at a negative one, and keeps the rest.
4. **`lists20.py`'s reason for F-247** said "three team tests and two demos". The worker reads it at the end of its brief, beside the rung's section that now names three; the reason names the third and fork 15.
5. **The header's review sentence.** `CLIMB-BATCH-19.md`'s header carries its review's sentence; this record now carries the same, with the review's base, what it read and ran, and its changes.
6. **`INDEX.md`'s line** for this review, after the record's line, in the form of climb batch 19's review's line.

## 3. What was checked and found right

**Rung I against P-153, word for word.** "Each integer type's `^` answers its own type at every exponent": `power.patch` writes the base's type on every integer `^`, in the component and the api: `Integral`'s `I` (`FortressLibrary.fss:721`, `.fsi:472`), `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN64` and `ZZ` at two declarations each (`fss:799-801`, `:892-894`, `:975-977`, `:1074-1076`; `fsi:524-525`, `:578`, `:636`, `:674`), `NN32` and `IntLiteral` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:460-462`, `:552-554`; `.fsi:167-168`, `:213-214`). Every line the patch touches holds `RR64` today, as the probe's section 1.1 lists them. "A negative exponent raises `IntegerOverflow` where the result is no integer, a base of 0 raises `DivisionByZero`, and the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power": rung I's natives section says exactly this for the six `Pow` classes, whose negative branches are at `Int.java:224-226`, `Long.java:236-238`, `NN32.java:231-233`, `UnsignedLong.java:231-233`, `BigNum.java:300-302` and `IntLiteral.java:250-252`, each `FFloat.make(1.0 / ...)` today; `Int.overflow()` is at `Int.java:258-261` and `integerOverflowException` at `WellKnownNames.java:86`; `DivisionByZero` is a library object (`FortressLibrary.fss:1782`, `.fsi:1113`). "A program that wants a fraction writes a float or rational base": `QQ`'s body becomes the probe's `typecase` (section 4), and the walk test asserts `(2/3)^(-1)` is `3/2` and `2.0^(-1)` is `0.5`. "Still to build": `fail[\ZZ32\]` at `fss:4543` is in the patch; the three team tests and the demos are fork 15.
- The question of fork 10. Under walk a numeral is an `FInt`, and `IntLiteral$Pow` is reached once in the suite, by `IntLiteralValue.fss:38` (the probe, section 1.1); so `2^(-1)` is `Int$Pow`'s, and raises. On the checker every integer numeral is `IntLiteral` (F-262), `prefix -` on a numeral is folded before the checker and `^` is not; so `2^(-1)` is `IntLiteral.^(self, b:IntLiteral)`, which is `self^(b.asZZ32)`, then `IntLiteral$Pow`: `IntegerOverflow` at 2, `1` at 1, `-1` at -1, as `IntLiteral`. Both are P-153's answer. The compiled path's own `ZZ32` power, `jIntExp` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss`, row 523), answers `0` and is outside the rung, held for phase 4 (fork 13; rows 441, 523).
- microGPT. Its own powers all have a float base: `10.0^(-12)` (`run-c4/src/MicroGptFlatQuick.fss:19-20`), `10.0^(-5)` and `10.0^(-8)` (`apl/mg/MicroGptApl.fss:27`), `10.0^e10` forms (`apl/mg/FlatData2.fss:41-43`), `b^e` with `b: RR64` (`apl/mg/AplMg.fss:37`). Its one integer power is `strToInt`'s `radix^(n-i)` with `i <- i0:n`, reached from `run-c4/src/FlatData.fss:34` and `apl/mg/FlatData2.fss:37` (F-247); `power.patch` changes that line's `fail` only, so a digit string's value is the same. Neither rung names a file under `explorations/`. The integer power probe measured the quick pair equal on E's text, and the array probe on A's two patches (`VERDICT: 7 PASS, 0 FAIL of 7`, both programs, both probes).

**Fork 7 and fork 8, the library's way.** `MultiplicativeRing`'s api writes `abstract getter one(): T` and `abstract opr TIMES(self, other:T): T` (`fsi:279-280`) where the component's members have no body (`fss:375-376`); its `^` at `fss:377` has no body either, and the landed second export error names it so: "Asbtract method ^ @ FortressLibrary.fss:377:5-378:1 is not declared in the API". Row 445 names the api's `other:ZZ64` in `QQ` and `MultiplicativeRing` and gives `AnyIntegral` as the fix. `RR64`'s api line is the component's `fss:487`, under the team's "Shouldn't need this extra declaration." Every type under the bound provides the power from the api's view: the five integer types through `Integral`'s api `opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):I` (`fsi:472`), `QQ` at `fsi:430`, `RR32` at `FortressBuiltin.fsi:110`, and `RR64` by the new line, which `Float` and `FloatLiteral` extend (`FortressBuiltin.fss:54`, `:194`). The planner's (a) shows the one gap without that line.

**Rung A against P-40.** `e3-rebased.patch` changes 17 `opr` lines and nothing else (`grep -c '^-opr'` and `'^+opr'` give 17 each; its two hunks are the api's `:1646-1680` and `:1771-1804`): the vector `+`, `-` and unary `-` lose `nat m`, the six vector products lose `nat m, nat p`, the eight matrix-vector, vector-matrix and scalar products lose `nat p`; the matrix `+` and `-` keep `n, m`, and the matrix product keeps `n, m, p`. The component already writes these products without the sizes (`fss:2603-2618` as `[\T, nat n\]`, `:2992-3014` as `[\T, nat n, nat m\]`), which is F-35's 2008 fix. The other eight unused sizes of the 25 stay, as rung A's "Not yours" says. The landed first export error's 17 entries are the 14 products (`fsi:1661-1676`, `:1774-1796`), the two `immutableArray` ranks (`:1500-1501`) and `array3()` (`:1860`): E3 clears 14, 4d two, 4f one, as the array probe measured. Fork 5: the component's comment around ranks 2 and 3 and their helpers is at `fss:2264-2269` and `:2275-2280` and stands at `a874948ac` (`:1941-1946` there); `ImmutableArray2` and `ImmutableArray3` are declared nowhere in `Library/` or `LibraryBuiltin/`. `ways.patch` is the probe's: `fill` and `tabulate` in `Vector` and `Matrix` with `StandardMutableArrayType`'s bodies (`fss:2313-2320`), `cast` (`fss:33-37`) around the five `Vector` and four `Matrix` bodies, the three factory arms, `Col` and `Row` with the subscript's 0-based value (`fss:2668-2675`), `matrix(v)` through `matrix[\T,s0,s1\]()`, the two api ranks in a comment, `array3(v)` after `array3()`. Its 19 sites are the landed list's: `:2526`, `:2528`, `:2529`, `:2530`, `:2532`, `:2596`, `:2598`, `:2839`, `:2841`, `:2842`, `:2843`, `:2903`, `:2908`, `:2977`, `:2551`, `:2562`, `:2946`, `:2697`, `:2701`. The eight element types of the guard are the bound's: `Vector` and `Matrix` take `T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }`, which `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64` and `ZZ` meet through `Integral`, and `QQ` (`fss:577-578`), `RR32` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:203-204`) and `RR64` (`fss:410-411`) directly; `IntLiteral` extends `Number` alone. No array body between `fss:2170` and `:3260` holds a `^`.

**The planner's departures from its brief.** The export check: `allAbstractsMadePublic` is `inComp.forall(...)` (`ExportChecker.scala:749`) and `equalListMembers` ends in `inAPI.forall(handleOne)` (`:787`); Scala's `forall` stops at the first `false`, and `handleOne` adds its cause only for the member it fails on, so each entry names one member; `:768-769` reports "missing members" when the api lists more than the component, before any member is compared. The measured new site: `ZZ`'s api declares no `zero` (`fsi:645-679`), `BigNum`'s api is `value object BigNum extends ZZ end` (`FortressBuiltin.fsi:223`), so from the api an `abstract getter zero(): I` in `Integral[\ZZ\]` has no concrete member there. `Integral` alone has 27 members with no body in the component (`fss:684-721`) and none written `abstract` in the api (`fsi:446-483`), against one named member in the error. So the mechanical part's extent is unknown and each line can reach another api: the evidence bears the hold-out out. Row 774: P-154 names walk's half as still to build; `boundsUnread` (`Constructor.java:722-737`) reads an `extends` entry without its clause, and no code reads the clause at an instance; PLAN's item 18 lists the row last, "which changes walk's values"; the record's probe-first default follows PLAN's method and moves no site.

**The distance and the count.** `distance-sites.tsv` (31 rows): the power's six are `:642` three times ("Could not check call to operator -", "Filter expressions ... must have type Boolean", "Function body has type RR64, but declared return type is QQ"), `:643`, `:4540` and `:4556`; A's are the 19 above and the first export error; left are the second export error, `:1463`, `:4368`, `:4374` and `List.fss:146`: 5. `checker-count.txt`: `#total 28`, every api 0; less A's 19 and I's 6: 3, at `:1463`, `:4368` and `:4374`, since `List.fss:146` is another component's. A alone 31 to 11 and 28 to 9; I alone 31 to 25 and 28 to 22. The second export error's 44 entries counted from the tsv; `MultiplicativeRing`'s is one, and `QQ`'s names `^` at `fsi:430` and `isNaN` at `fss:589`, so it narrows to `isNaN` after fork 8. `distance.txt` gives `#seconds 153`; the count stage's 64.5 s is `reviews/batch-19-review.md:28`.

**The team lines a rung rewrites, each on the review list with its before and after.** `realArith.fss:54` and `:57` (`1.2246467991473532 TIMES 10^(-16)`), `compoundArray.fss:17-18`, `:27`, `:32` and `:33-34` (`7.07106781186547462 10^(-1)`, `3 10^(-2)`, `3.14 10^(-2)`), `simpleExp.fss:18-20`, `BiCGSTAB.fss:211` and `BiCGSTAB2.fss:198` (`er0 = 1.0 10^(-4)`), `npbft.fss:130`. `compoundArray.fss:26` and `:31` raise `v`, an `RR64`, and stay. Fork 15 and the manifest's point for I ask for each line's before and after, and "Team lines changed" names the files. The tests come first on each rung: I's walk test fails on the base (`2^(-1)` is `0.5`, `0^(-1)` `Infinity`, the probe's section 1.1), the respelled team tests are seen passing on the base, `QQPowerExponent` fails on the base by `FBigNum.java:48-50`; A's guard passes before and after, and its distance stage is its test, as "its test is the stage: yes" says. The tests the record names exist: `PowChooseLcmRungE` with `overflows` at `:6-12`, `XXXQQPowerExponent`, `InferResultOnlyIfWithoutElse`, `XXXArrayInferredElementVectorWalk`, `ArrayFactoryAbstractNumber`, `IntLiteralValue`, `FlatTowerRungF`, `NumeralTest`, `QuickCheckTest`, `RationalTest` (its rational bases at `:707-712`), `BooleanOps`.

**The patches.** Each applies alone to `main`; in the gather's order `power.patch`, `ways.patch` (hunks 5 to 7 at offset 2) and `e3-rebased.patch` (offsets 5 and 7) apply together, 4 files, +88 -62; `export-abstract.patch` applies on top (offset 1). The record's "1 to 7 lines" holds.

**The specification.** `basic-integers.tex:298-320` is the revision box, "This chapter does not give it." at `:320`; `:524-529` the method entry, "Exponentiation of an integer to a nonnegative integer power produces an integer result" at `:527`; `changes.tex:882-1013` "The integer trait", "its power on integers is another method, returning a floating-point value" at `:902-903`, "The revised text of \secref{basic-integers} does not give it." at `:913`; `:4034` "The result of an integer raised to a negative power is not yet given"; `opr-overview.tex:73` "This operation is defined in the usual way on numerals"; `default-libraries.tex:27` inputs the rendered api; `arrays-distributed.tex:53-55` is the table's `fill` and `tabulate`; `changes.tex:1245-1281` "Initializing an array from a function".

**The gate figures the record cites.** `summary.txt`: `testSystem` shards 167, 167, 161 and 169 (664); the compiler track 1,280, the library track 86, the other-compiler track 263, `testSpecData` 130; 42 `# atomic` lines; microGPT's quick pair 44 s and 36 s (`reviews/batch-19-review.md:459`). The cost: batch 19 wrote 3.82M over 12 agents in 2 h 56 min, 0.35M for the VM restart (`reviews/batch-19-review.md:42`, `:60`).

**The manifest.** `lists20.py`: 67 keys, I 37 with 13 checks (about 27.8K tokens), A 30 with 11 checks (about 34.8K), every key matching one place, 0 problems. `gen20.py`: I 11,714 and A 8,115 characters of section after the fixes, 9 and 8 points. `check20.js` on the fixed record: every check ok, 0 problems; the scatter IA by expected minutes (120, 90); no `landsOnlyWith`, no checker count, no gate step, no `LEDGER_FROM`; the tracked script's block differs from the generated one, as it should before step 2 of "Before the launch". `workflow-scenarios.js` on the spliced scratch copy: 0 problems. Section 5's steps follow the manual's "Before the launch" in its order.

**The decisions, facts and rows cited.** P-153, P-40, P-154, P-26, P-80, P-73, P-76, P-27, P-87, P-85, P-39, P-103, P-124, P-30, P-90, P-151 and P-45 say what the record says of them; F-241, F-247, F-260, F-262, F-35, F-53 and F-240 too. Rows 438, 441, 445, 747, 523, 678, 465, 685, 731, 632, 774, 773 and 786 claim what the record says. The digest's grouping of the 31 (`reviews/digest-2026-10-19.md`, section 2) is the record's. PLAN's item 18 lists the candidates as section 4 has them, row 774 last, and item 46 with no default; the review list "Climb batch 19" holds `tint` and gather.2.

## 4. What was weighed and left as drafted

- `simpleExp`'s comment, "that Int and Long exponentiation work (largely) as expected", stays over a test whose bases become floats (fork 15). The record's reason stands: the rung's own walk test checks the integer bases, and the comment is the team's. A reader of the file alone is misled; the review list's before-and-after lines say why.
- `not_passing_yet/tree.fss:54-73` writes `10^(-1)` scales twenty times. No suite runs the folder, P-153 names the tests the suites run, and the file does not pass for other reasons. Left out of the rung; noted for the coordinator.
- The compiled path's own `2^(-1)` stays `0`, through `jIntExp`, until phase 4's natives (fork 13; rows 441, 523). The rung's "Not yours" keeps it out, and the row's note records the half fixed.
- Fork 11 at `ZZ`: `BigInteger.pow` takes an `int` exponent, so a `ZZ` exponent beyond 31 bits cannot be computed at any base but 0, 1 and -1; `IntegerOverflow` there is the rule the record gives, and the worker says what it chose.
- The method entry's `:524-529` opens on the team's `%` comment line and closes on the entry's last sentence; the revision box's `:298-320` and Appendix I's `:882-1013` are exact.
- The guard's column and row at a base above 0: right to ask, since the probe's M1 read the column of a 0-based array only, and the landed `Col` and `Row` take `self[(b0,i1)#(s0,1)]` and `self[(i0,b1)#(1,s1)]` through the 0-based subscript. The unsigned types' unary minus is the worker's to state, as the record says.
- Fork 7's (c) over (b): (b) leaves the entry for the modifier alone, and `abstract` is what the api writes for the trait's other bodiless members; (c) is measured. Left.
- The cost and the time (about 3.4M, about 3 hours): batch 19's figures with one rung of patches to apply; no better estimate is at hand.
